text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Bank insurer ING's British unit Barings seeks to use mergers and acquisitions expertise in European market. (p1)
- Netherlands loses grip on port export market due to ongoing swine fever epidemic. (p1)
- Economic Affairs and Finance Ministeries clashed over technolease deals between Philips and Rabobank, former Economic Affairs Minister told parliamentary committee.
- Food co-op Cosun sees net profit growth accelerate in 1996. (p3).
- Union FNV sells 51 pct stake in insurer Reaal for friendly price (p3)
- Rating bureau Moody's confirms insurer Aegon's credit rating. (p3)
- Automation company Baan threatens to leave Netherlands for tax haven, Ireland. (p3)
- Dutch manufacturing output rises more than five percent in March from January and February. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch consumer electronics company BCC sold for 105 million guilders to Britain's Kingfisher. (p2)
- ING reveals outstanding bad debts of 4.7 billion guilders. (p2).
- Builder HBG's unit HAM to dredge for salt in Jordan. (p2)
- Employers and unions in engineering sector talk about slim-lining early retirement scheme. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- The Hague prepares for U.S. president Bill Clinton's visit on Tuesday. (p1)
- Dutch wages to rise an average 2.4 percent this year from 1.6 percent in 1996. (p1)
- Shortage of lower technical staff forces DAF Trucks to hire workers in Belgium.
- Dutch textile industry slowly recovers; sector carefully optimistic about 1997.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Engineering bureaus, hoping to play part in developing national airport in sea, tumble over each other with what they think is best solution. (p1)
- Port of Rotterdam must economise, says city's advisory board. (p11)
TROUW
- Education minister tries to fight looming shortage of technical workers with proposal to concentrate technical education in 20 technocentres. (p3)
- Business investigator Pieter Lakeman calls for probe into possible corruption in sale of aircraft maker Fokker to Germany's DASA. (p7)
